eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs project a daytime high in the mid-70s for Chicago on May 17, well above the 64°F threshold that currently carries 99.7% implied probability. Southerly flow ahead of a modest trough is expected to advect warmer air masses northward, consistent with climatological warming observed since early May and seasonal normals near 71°F. Short-range deterministic and probabilistic forecasts show minimal spread, with only modest cloud cover or isolated showers likely to trim afternoon peaks by a few degrees at most. A rapid, unforecasted cold-air intrusion or major model bust would be required to push the observed high below 64°F, an outcome historical May analogs render highly improbable within the next 48 hours.
